rawFindings.title: Use of injector inside createKarmaMiddleware causes incompatibility with existing $inject annotations and may break DI behavior
rawFindings.explanation: The createKarmaMiddleware function was changed to take an injector parameter and retrieve config values from it inside the returned middleware. The prior version took these config values as parameters directly with $inject annotations. This change breaks the previously declared $inject array for dependency injection, potentially breaking DI in setups relying on $inject annotations or on direct parameters for config values.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert createKarmaMiddleware signature to accept config.client, config.customContextFile, and config.customDebugFile as separate parameters instead of using injector inside the middleware. Alternatively, update the $inject array and DI setup accordingly to inject the injector and handle config retrieval consistently.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Starting Karma server with the new middleware setup where DI relies on $inject annotations can cause errors or missing configuration values because the injector is not injected properly or config client values are not found at runtime.

rawFindings.title: Possible missing log debug for serving custom files in createKarmaMiddleware
rawFindings.explanation: The new code added several log.debug lines for debugging serving customContextFile and customDebugFile but these logs might expose internal urls or client configuration, which could lead to verbose or sensitive information leaking in logs if not carefully controlled.
rawFindings.suggestion: Review the necessity and content of debug logs added at lines 125, 131, 135 to verify that sensitive information is not logged, and optionally remove or secure these logs for production environments.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Debug logs could reveal sensitive internal file paths or configuration values during request handling, potentially leaking information to log files.
